text:
OpenAI released o3 and o4-mini on April 16, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. The launch signaled a shift in frontier reasoning models toward integrating vision directly into the model architecture rather than bolting it on, and incorporating native tool use (such as web search and code interpreter) trained into the model itself [Source: ev-1]. It also marked OpenAI’s first private chain-of-thought policy, where reasoning tokens are not exposed to API callers [Source: ev-1].

Strategically, with GPT-5 not yet shipping, OpenAI used this release to defend its position at the frontier against DeepSeek's R1 cost shock and Anthropic's agentic-coding push [Source: ev-1]. The launch reframed frontier capability as "tool-using reasoning at commodity prices," evidenced by o4-mini’s pricing of $1.10 per million input tokens and $4.40 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1]. Additionally, the models introduced a technique called budget forcing, which uses a fixed maximum thought budget but allows for task-adaptive (dynamic) compute so that harder questions require longer thinking times [Source: ev-1].

The release also demonstrated significant performance improvements, with o3 setting a record on the ARC-AGI benchmark by achieving approximately 87.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at high compute, meeting or exceeding the ~85% human baseline as the first model to do so [Source: ev-1]. The launch was API-first, making both models available to developers from day one, although o3 was not included in the ChatGPT app until later [Source: ev-1].
